content: ***The Off-Season*** is the sixth studio album[3] by American rapper [J. Cole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Cole). It was released on May 14, 2021, by [Dreamville Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamville_Records), [Roc Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roc_Nation) and [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records). The album was executive produced by Cole, [Ibrahim Hamad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibrahim_Hamad_(music_executive)), and [T-Minus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-Minus_(record_producer)). It also features guest vocals from [Morray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morray), [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage), [Lil Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Baby), [Bas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bas_(rapper)), and [6lack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6lack). It became Cole's first album since 2013's *[Born Sinner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_Sinner)* to contain guest features. Production was handled by multiple producers, including Cole himself, T-Minus, [Timbaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbaland), [Boi-1da](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boi-1da), [Frank Dukes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Dukes), [DJ Dahi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Dahi), [Tae Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tae_Beast), and [Jake One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_One), among others.[4]

*The Off-Season* was supported by one [single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_(music)), "[My Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Life_(J._Cole,_21_Savage_and_Morray_song))", and [promotional singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotional_recording), "[The Climb Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Climb_Back)" and "[Interlude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interlude_(J._Cole_song))". *The Off-Season* was accompanied by a twelve-minute short film upon its release titled, *[Applying Pressure: The Off-Season Documentary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applying_Pressure:_The_Off-Season_Documentary)*.

*The Off-Season* received positive reviews from critics and topped the US [*Billboard* 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200). It sold 282,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_units) in its first week, earning Cole his sixth consecutive number-one album in the country. At the time of its release, *The Off-Season* achieved the largest streaming week of 2021, accumulating over 325.5 million streams. Four songs from *The Off-Season* debuted in the top ten on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100); every song on the album charted in the top forty. The album scored a nomination for [Best Rap Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap_Album) at the [64th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/64th_Annual_Grammy_Awards). Also, "[Pride Is the Devil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Is_the_Devil)" was nominated for [Best Melodic Rap Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Melodic_Rap_Performance), while "My Life" was nominated for [Best Rap Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Song) and [Best Rap Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Performance).

sections.heading: Background
content: On August 7, 2018, Cole released "[Album of the Year (Freestyle)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album_of_the_Year_(Freestyle))",[5] accompanied by a music video. Cole announced *The Off-Season*,[5] which will precede the release of what was originally planned to be his sixth studio album, *[The Fall-Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fall-Off)*. In the description to the video, it reads: "The Off Season coming soon... All roads lead to The Fall Off - Cole".[6] In an interview with *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_(magazine))* in September 2018, Cole announced his plans to take off time in 2019 from touring to finish work on *The Off-Season*, *The Fall-Off*, and his [Kill Edward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kill_Edward) project.[7]

On December 29, 2020, Cole posted a photo on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram) where he documented a list titled, "The Fall Off Era". On the list crossed out, was features and *[Revenge of the Dreamers III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revenge_of_the_Dreamers_III)*. Also listed, but not crossed out was two projects, *The Off-Season* and *It's a Boy*, which he intends to release ahead of *The Fall-Off*. The caption of the post read: "I still got some goals I gotta check off for' I scram...", alluding to a potential retirement.[8]

sections.heading: Recording and production
content: As one of the executive producers of the album, [T-Minus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-Minus_(record_producer)) began producing with Cole in 2017, collaborating on "[Kevin's Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin's_Heart)", "[Middle Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Child)", and "[Lion King on Ice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lion_King_on_Ice)". He spoke on producing for Cole in an interview saying, "Cole is very much a producer, so he likes to direct where the music is going as far as arrangement, or the bounce, or the feeling that he wants to have. So he gave me a bunch of ideas and pointers for what he wanted to do."[9] When asked about Cole's creative mindset for the mixtape, he said: "Cole is tapped into every aspect of the creation of the record. He writes all of his own music, writes all of the songs. He produces, he mixes; he's super involved [...] he's just that guy who's very grounded when it comes to the creation of the entire record, which is dope because when I create with him, he's very much directing where he wants the record to go."[9]

sections.heading: Artwork and title
content: The cover art was organized by Dreamville's creative director Felton Brown and shot in [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina) by Justin Francis.[10] The artwork shows Cole standing in front of a basketball hoop on fire, referencing the basketball theme on the covers of his mixtapes *[The Warm Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Warm_Up)* (2009) and *[Friday Night Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friday_Night_Lights_(mixtape))* (2010), and debut album *[Cole World: The Sideline Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_World:_The_Sideline_Story)* (2011).[11] Brown told *[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_Magazine)* magazine:

Cole signed a contract with the [Rwanda Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriots_BBC) in the [Basketball Africa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_Africa_League).[13] Cole was also featured on the cover of the American basketball magazine *[Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slam_(magazine))* for the May 2021 issue. sections.heading: Release and promotion
content: On November 8, 2018, Cole made a playlist on streaming services titled, *Where the fuck is The Off Season*, which contains all of his 2018 features. The playlist also includes [Jeezy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeezy)'s song "American Dream" (2017), J. Cole's singles "[Everybody Dies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody_Dies_(J._Cole_song))" (2016), "[False Prophets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/False_Prophets_(song))" (2016), "[High for Hours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_for_Hours)" (2017), "[Album of the Year (Freestyle)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album_of_the_Year_(Freestyle))" (2018), and "[1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_(J._Cole_song))" (2018).[15]

On May 4, 2021, J. Cole officially announced the release date of the album on social media, and revealed the artwork.[16][17][18] On May 10, 2021, Cole released a documentary titled, *[Applying Pressure: The Off-Season Documentary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applying_Pressure:_The_Off-Season_Documentary)* via [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube).[19] The short film is divided into four chapters where Cole shares a behind the scenes look in the studio as well as private moments during the album's creating process. The film was executive produced by Cole himself, Ibrahim Hamad, and Tripp Kramer, and directed by Scott Lazer. The film features a cameo from fellow rapper [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage).[20][21] While describing the inspiration of the mixtape, Cole said in the documentary:
On May 13, 2021, hours prior to its release, Cole revealed the album's tracklist and production credits via social media.[23]

content.heading: Tour
content: To further promote the album, Cole announced [The Off-Season Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Off-Season_Tour) on June 22, 2021. The tour included 20 North American dates, and began on September 24, 2021 in [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami) and concluded on April 3, 2022, in [Raleigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raleigh,_North_Carolina) at the Dreamville festival. 21 Savage served as the co-headliner and [Morray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morray) served as their supporting act on the tour.[24]

content.heading: Singles
content: "[My Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Life_(J._Cole,_21_Savage_and_Morray_song))", with 21 Savage and Morray, impacted [rhythmic contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_contemporary) radio in the United States on May 25, 2021, as the album's first official radio [single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_(music)).[25][26] It debuted and peaked at number two on the Hot 100.[27]

content.heading: Other songs
content: On July 22, 2020, Cole released "[The Climb Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Climb_Back)" as a dual single along with, "[Lion King on Ice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lion_King_on_Ice)", under the title *[Lewis Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Street)*. According to Cole, the two songs were originally intended to be the first singles from his upcoming album *The Fall-Off*. "The Climb Back" is included on the album.[28]

On May 7, 2021, Cole released "[Interlude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interlude_(J._Cole_song))", the first [promotional single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotional_single) from the album, initially planning on releasing the album all at once with no singles prior to its release, as he had done in the past starting with his third studio album, *[2014 Forest Hills Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Forest_Hills_Drive)*. The interlude was produced by [T-Minus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-Minus_(record_producer)), Tommy Parker, and Cole himself.[29] In the US, the song debuted with 8.5 million on-demand audio streams in its first day.[30] It also reached number one on US [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music) in less than a day.[31] "Interlude" debuted and peaked at number eight on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100).[27]

On May 17, 2021, the music video was released for the song, "[Amari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amari_(song))",[32] the video was directed by [Raleigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raleigh,_North_Carolina)-based rapper [Mez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mez_(rapper)), who also directed the music video for Cole's 2019 hit and multi-platinum single, "[Middle Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Child)".[33][34] Cole released the music video for the song, "Applying Pressure"[35] on May 25, 2021, and a music video for "Punchin' the Clock" on June 3, 2021.[36] Both videos were directed by Scott Lazer and produced by Tripp Kramer. "Applying Pressure" features an appearance from rapper [Dave East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_East), who Cole also made a reference to in the song. All three music videos were filmed in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City).[37]

sections.heading: Critical reception
content: *The Off-Season* was met with positive reception from music critics. At [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic), which assigns a [normalized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_score) rating out of 100 to reviews from professional publications, the album received an [average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean) score of 76, based on ten reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews".[39] Aggregator AnyDecentMusic? gave it 7.2 out of 10, based on their assessment of the critical consensus.[38]

*[Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_(magazine))* gave the album a positive review saying, Cole "reached astronomical heights. Fortunately for fans, they did not have to wait long, and the North Carolina rapper did not disappoint." The writer continued to say "*The Off-Season* is a solid project with no expiration date and can easily be digested for months and years to come. While some fans may be eager for more, *The Off-Season* is a great appetiser for the main dish and contains just enough for those that have been waiting for three years on The Real."[41] Writing for *[Exclaim!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exclaim!)*, Luke Fox praised the album, calling Cole "refocused and rejuvenated", he continued saying: "If 2018's concept-heavy, dangerously didactic *[KOD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KOD_(album))* was Cole drifting into the player-coach stage of his career, *The Off-Season* is Cole lacing up squeaky high-tops and drilling 100,000 hours of threes".[42]

*[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine))'*s Brandon Yu wrote the following: "Particularly as hip-hop continues to transform as the new pop, Cole, a steadfast rap traditionalist now a good decade into his career, might appear as a relic (for some fans, the generation-war of his "[1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_(J._Cole_song))" read as this very truth). On "*The Off-Season*," he is burnishing a reputation as a lingering titan. If "*The Off-Season*" is Cole's first record of The Fall Off Era, he appears far from ready to bow out, nor should he be."[50] Yoh Phillips of *[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_(magazine))* called the album a "workout session", he wrote, "*The Off-Season* sets Cole up to create the conversation about his place in rap history, and he'll need to deliver a blockbuster finale to fulfill the premonition he made 11 years ago on "[Last Call](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Warm_Up)."[51] Craig Jenkins of *[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_(magazine))* said: "As the title suggests, *The Off-Season* is sort of a training montage, a blade-sharpening exercise like [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_(musician))'s *[If You're Reading This It's Too Late](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_You're_Reading_This_It's_Too_Late)* in its core objective of showing the work it takes to stay on top while cultivating buzz for a future release (in this case, Cole's forthcoming *The Fall-Off*) – and maybe notching a few more hit records along the way."[52] Writing for [AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic), Fred Thomas said, "The album is a varied selection with solid performances and production throughout. Much like the title suggests, *The Off-Season* feels like Cole running through different exercises as he gets in shape for something bigger."[40]

sections.heading: Commercial performance
content: On the day of its release, *The Off-Season* broke [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify)'s one-day streaming record for 2021 up until that point with 62 million streams.[27] In the United States, the album debuted at number one on the US [*Billboard* 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200), earning 282,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_units) (including 37,000 copies as pure album sales) in its first week.[71] This became Cole's seventh US number one album on the chart.[71] At the time of its release, *The Off-Season* achieved the largest streaming week of 2021, accumulating over 325.5 million on-demand streams of the album's 12 tracks, surpassing [Morgan Wallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Wallen)’s *[Dangerous: The Double Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerous:_The_Double_Album)* which debuted with 240.18 million streams for its 30 songs in its first week.[71] The project also earned the largest week of 2021 for a hip-hop album, until being surpassed by [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West)’s album *[Donda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donda_(album)).*[72] and [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_(musician))'s album *[Certified Lover Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Lover_Boy_(album))*.[73] In its second week, the album dropped to number two on the chart, earning an additional 92,000 units, while losing the number one position to [Olivia Rodrigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Rodrigo)'s debut album, [*Sour*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sour_(album)).[74] In its third week, the album dropped to number three on the chart, earning 58,000 more units.[75] In its fourth week, the album dropped to number four on the chart, earning 44,000 units.[76] As of December 2021, the album has earned over 1,000,000 album-equivalent units in the United States.[77]

Four songs from *The Off-Season* debuted in the top ten on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100), with "[My Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Life_(J._Cole,_21_Savage_and_Morray_song))" (at 2), "[Amari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amari_(song))" (at 5), "[Pride Is the Devil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_Is_the_Devil)" (at 7), and "[95 South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/95_South_(song))" (at 8). [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_(musician)), [Juice WRLD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juice_WRLD), [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne) & [Lil Uzi Vert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Uzi_Vert) are the only other artists to have four songs debut in the top ten. "[Interlude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interlude_(J._Cole_song))" debuted at number eight the previous week giving the album five top ten singles.[78] Every song on the album charted in the top forty on the Hot 100.[79]
